llm_response.content:
Below is a complete empirical plan tailored to this setting, using only the information you provided and proposing what I would do to identify causal effects.

1. Identification Strategy

Primary: Staggered difference-in-differences (DID) with an event-study
- Unit of treatment: bank.
- Treatment: receipt of CPP funds.
- Design: bank-by-quarter panel with bank fixed effects and calendar-quarter fixed effects; event-time coefficients around bank-specific funding dates. For loan-level outcomes (HMDA, DealScan), I leverage within-market-by-time comparisons so that identification comes from treated vs. control banks operating in the same local market and quarter (county×quarter FE in HMDA; borrower-industry×quarter FE or borrower×quarter FE in DealScan when feasible).
- Estimator: Sun–Abraham or Callaway–Sant’Anna to handle staggered adoption and heterogeneous treatment effects.

Secondary: IV-DID using regulator approval propensity
- Motivation: address residual selection in approval/acceptance.
- Instrument: leave-one-out approval propensity of the primary regulator in the bank’s regulator×district (or regulator×state)×application-month cohort. Intuition: conditional on observables and application, differences in regulator approval “toughness”/workload generate quasi-exogenous variation in receipt and timing.
- Estimation: two-stage least squares in a bank×quarter panel with bank and time FE, instrumenting the treatment indicator (and/or dose: CPP dollars/Assets) with regulator-propensity interacted with post-application exposure.

Tertiary: Difference-in-difference-in-differences (DDD) within risk segments
- HMDA: compare changes in approval behavior for higher-risk applicants vs. lower-risk applicants within the same county×quarter as an additional layer that nets out local demand shocks. The interaction Treat×Post×HighRisk is the coefficient of interest.
- DealScan: analogous DDD using riskier loan terms (e.g., covenant-lite, unsecured/subordinated, lower-rated borrowers) vs. safer terms within borrower-industry×quarter.

Rationale
- DID/event study is natural for staggered receipt of CPP and rich pre-period (2006–2008Q3).
- Market×time FE at loan level sharply improves comparability by conditioning on local credit demand and shocks.
- IV-DID strengthens causal inference against approval endogeneity and endogenous timing.
- DDD isolates risk-mix shifts, not just volume changes.


2. Treatment and Control

- Treatment variable:
  - Main: Treated_bt = 1 starting the first full calendar quarter after bank b receives CPP funds (funding date from filings); remains 1 thereafter.
  - Alternative dose: CPPAmount_b / Assets_b, pre-defined at first receipt; or quarterly cumulative outstanding CPP / assets.
- Control group:
  - Baseline: Eligible banks that never receive CPP in 2008–2010.
  - Event-study controls: also include not-yet-treated banks up to their treatment dates.
  - Applicant-only robustness: Compare approved-and-funded vs. denied or approved-but-declined applicants.
- Treatment timing / event date:
  - Event time 0 = the first quarter in which CPP funds are on balance sheet (or the immediately following quarter for accounting clean timing). Leads and lags up to ±8 quarters (as data allow).
- IV construction:
  - Z_bm = leave-one-out approval rate for bank b’s primary regulator r in regulator×district (or regulator×state) and application-month m among all other applicants in that cohort. Use cohort-month relative to each bank’s application month.
  - For dose, interact Z_bm with pre-CPP risk-weighted assets to instrument CPP dollars/Assets.


3. Key Identifying Assumptions

A. DID/event study assumptions
- Parallel pre-trends: In absence of CPP, treated and control banks would have followed similar trends in outcomes after conditioning on bank FE, calendar-quarter FE, and rich controls; and, at loan-level, within the same market×time.
  - Plausibility: We can test via event-study leads; loan-level specifications with county×quarter FE are particularly demanding and reduce concerns about local demand confounders.
- No anticipatory behavioral change prior to funding date (or minimal within estimation bandwidth).
  - Plausibility: Announced 10/14/2008, but bank-specific approval and funding dates differ; we will include multiple pre-leads. We can also drop the weeks spanning the announcement and use first funds-on-balance-sheet quarter to mitigate pure announcement effects.
- Stable composition and SUTVA/no spillovers within market×time (or small enough).
  - Plausibility: Spillovers are possible if untreated competitors react to treated banks. Market×quarter FE absorb common shocks, but competitive responses could attenuate or bias effects. We will test for spillovers directly.

B. IV-DID assumptions
- Relevance: Regulator approval propensity strongly predicts CPP receipt (and timing/dose) conditional on bank and time FE.
- Exclusion: Conditional on bank FE, time FE, and observables, regulator approval propensity affects lending/investment risk only via CPP receipt, not through other regulator-driven changes contemporaneous with CPP.
  - Plausibility: Primary regulators differ systematically; hence we use leave-one-out within regulator×district×month and control for regulator×quarter FE and rich pre-crisis bank characteristics and trends.
- Monotonicity: For a given bank, a higher regulator propensity does not make receipt less likely (no defiers).
  - Plausibility: Reasonable if “toughness”/workload differences shift approval probability in a common direction.


4. Threats to Identification and Mitigations

1) Selection into application/approval/acceptance
- Threat: More distressed or more aggressive banks may self-select into CPP or be differentially approved.
- Mitigations:
  - Restrict to universe of CPP-eligible publicly traded institutions.
  - Applicant-only DID comparing approved+funded vs. denied/declined.
  - Rich pre-period controls and bank fixed effects; bank-specific linear trends as robustness.
  - Event-study pre-trend tests.
  - IV-DID using regulator propensity (first stage F-stat checked; include regulator×quarter FE; placebo tests using pre-CPP periods with pseudo instruments).

2) Concurrent crisis programs and shocks (TLGP, Fed facilities, QE, supervisory forbearance)
- Threat: Other supports may coincide with treatment and contaminate effects.
- Mitigations:
  - Control for use/eligibility of TLGP and discount window/PDCF/TAF from public disclosures where available; or include bank exposure to these programs interacted with time.
  - Calendar-quarter FE absorb macro shocks; market×quarter FE at loan-level absorb local conditions.
  - Exclude the 17 CAP-stress-tested institutions and perform size-specific subsamples.

3) Spillovers within markets
- Threat: Untreated banks in treated markets adjust behavior, biasing DID.
- Mitigations:
  - Include county×quarter FE in HMDA models; borrower-industry×quarter or borrower×quarter FE in DealScan.
  - Explicit spillover test: instrument market-level treated share and examine untreated banks’ behaviors; re-estimate excluding markets with high treated penetration.
  - Clustered standard errors at bank; two-way cluster (bank and market) in loan-level models.

4) Measurement of “risk-taking”
- Threat: Stock measures blend legacy assets with new risk-taking; HMDA lacks FICO/LTV.
- Mitigations:
  - Focus on flow measures: approval rates and loan terms on new originations (HMDA, DealScan).
  - Define HMDA risk using high loan-amount-to-income (LAI), low-income borrowers, investor/non-owner-occupied, higher-priced loans (rate spread indicator pre-2010), subprime lender flag, and local house price collapse (high-decline tracts).
  - For investments: use changes in securities mix (e.g., private-label MBS/ABS share, trading assets), Level 2/3 fair-value exposures where available, and duration exposure from reports.


5. R Code Outline

Assumptions:
- bank_quarter.csv: bank_id, quarter, assets, tier1_cap_ratio, rwa, securities_breakdown, chargeoffs, dd_merton, zscore, tlgp_use, fed_facility_use, regulator_id, regulator_district, cpp_received_date, cpp_amount
- cpp_applications.csv: bank_id, applied_date, approved_date, accepted_date, funded_date, approval_status, acceptance_status
- hmda_2006_2010.csv: loan_id, lender_id (mapped to bank_id), quarter, county_fips, applicant_income, loan_amount, lien_status, occupancy, rate_spread, action_taken (approve=1/deny=0), race_ethnicity, purpose
- dealscan_2006_2010.csv: facility_id, lead_arranger_bank_id, quarter, borrower_id, borrower_rating, spread_bps, unsecured, subordinated, covlite, maturity_months, purpose, industry
- county_controls.csv: county_fips, quarter, unemployment_rate, usps_vacancy, hpi_change
- regulator_props.csv: regulator_id, regulator_district, application_month, loo_approval_rate

Packages: data.table, fixest, sandwich, clubSandwich, did (or fixest sunab), ivreg

Note: This is an outline; paths/variable names may need adjustment.

R code:

# Load packages
library(data.table)
library(fixest)
library(lubridate)
library(did)         # optional for Callaway-Sant'Anna
library(ivreg)       # alternative IV
library(modelsummary)

# 1) Load data
bank <- fread("bank_quarter.csv")
cpp <- fread("cpp_applications.csv")
hmda <- fread("hmda_2006_2010.csv")
deals <- fread("dealscan_2006_2010.csv")
county <- fread("county_controls.csv")
regprop <- fread("regulator_props.csv")

# 2) Prepare bank-quarter panel and treatment
bank[, quarter := as.yearqtr(quarter)]
cpp[, funded_qtr := as.yearqtr(funded_date)]
cpp[, approved_qtr := as.yearqtr(approved_date)]
cpp[, applied_qtr  := as.yearqtr(applied_date)]

# Merge CPP info
bank <- merge(bank, cpp[, .(bank_id, funded_qtr, approved_qtr, applied_qtr, approval_status, acceptance_status)], 
              by = "bank_id", all.x = TRUE)

# Define treatment timing: first quarter with funds on BS; treat from next full quarter if needed
bank[, treat_start := funded_qtr]
bank[, treat := as.integer(!is.na(treat_start) & quarter >= treat_start)]

# Event time for Sun-Abraham
bank[, etime := ifelse(!is.na(treat_start), as.integer((as.yearqtr(quarter) - treat_start) * 4), NA_integer_)]

# Controls: size and pretrends
setorder(bank, bank_id, quarter)
bank[, ln_assets := log(assets)]
bank[, pre_roa := shift(chargeoffs, 4, type = "lag"), by = bank_id]  # placeholder for pre-outcome; adjust as needed

# 3) Bank-level event study: investment risk (e.g., risky securities share)
# Example outcome construction (placeholder variable names)
# Create risky securities share: private-label MBS + trading assets over total securities
bank[, risky_sec_share := (get("securities_priv_label_mbs") + get("securities_trading")) / pmax(get("securities_total"), 1)]

# Estimate Sun-Abraham event study
# sunab(G, T): G=treat_start, T=quarter index as integer; build integer time
bank[, q_index := as.integer((quarter - min(quarter)) * 4) + 1]
bank[, g_index := ifelse(!is.na(treat_start), as.integer((treat_start - min(quarter)) * 4) + 1, NA_integer_)]

es1 <- feols(risky_sec_share ~ sunab(g_index, q_index) + ln_assets | bank_id + quarter, 
             data = bank, cluster = ~ bank_id)
etable(es1, dict = c("sunab"="Event time"), se.below = TRUE)

# 4) HMDA loan-level DDD: approval propensity for higher-risk applicants
# Define high-risk: top quartile loan-amount-to-income within county×year; plus non-owner-occupied or rate-spread
hmda[, year := year(as.Date(paste0(substr(quarter,1,4), "-01-01")))]
hmda[, lai := loan_amount / pmax(applicant_income, 1)]
hmda <- merge(hmda, bank[, .(bank_id, quarter, treat)], 
              by.x = c("lender_id","quarter"), by.y = c("bank_id","quarter"), all.x = TRUE)

# Compute county-year lai quartile cutoff
hmda[, lai_q := cut(lai, breaks = quantile(lai, probs = c(0, .75, 1), na.rm = TRUE), labels = c("low","high"), include.lowest = TRUE), 
     by = .(county_fips, year)]
hmda[, high_risk := as.integer(lai_q == "high" | occupancy == "Investor" | rate_spread == 1)]

# Outcome: approval (1=approved)
hmda[, approve := as.integer(action_taken == 1)]

# County×quarter FE via i() in fixest; lender FE absorb time-invariant lender traits
hmda_mod <- feols(approve ~ treat*high_risk + high_risk + 
                    i(county_fips, quarter) + i(lender_id) + 
                    log(loan_amount) + log(pmax(applicant_income,1)) |
                    0,
                  data = hmda, cluster = ~ lender_id)

etable(hmda_mod)

# 5) DealScan: riskier loan terms
# Merge treatment
deals <- merge(deals, bank[, .(bank_id, quarter, treat)], 
               by.x = c("lead_arranger_bank_id","quarter"), by.y = c("bank_id","quarter"), all.x = TRUE)
# Define risk: cov-lite or unsecured/subordinated or spread
deals[, risky_term := as.integer(covlite == 1 | unsecured == 1 | subordinated == 1)]
deal_mod <- feols(risky_term ~ treat + i(industry, quarter) + i(lead_arranger_bank_id) + 
                    log(pmax(spread_bps,1)) + as.factor(borrower_rating),
                  data = deals, cluster = ~ lead_arranger_bank_id)
etable(deal_mod)

# 6) Overall default risk (z-score or market DD) and interaction with capital
# Construct capital change after treatment
bank[, post := as.integer(quarter >= treat_start)]
bank[, d_tier1 := tier1_cap_ratio - shift(tier1_cap_ratio, 1), by = bank_id]

# Interaction model: default risk on treat, capital ratio and interaction
z_mod <- feols(zscore ~ treat + tier1_cap_ratio + treat:tier1_cap_ratio + ln_assets | bank_id + quarter,
               data = bank, cluster = ~ bank_id)
etable(z_mod)

# 7) IV-DID: instrument treat or dose with regulator approval propensity
# Merge regulator propensity by application-month cohort
cpp[, app_month := format(applied_date, "%Y-%m")]
regprop[, app_month := as.character(app_month)]
cpp <- merge(cpp, regprop, 
             by = c("regulator_id","regulator_district","app_month"), all.x = TRUE)

bank <- merge(bank, cpp[, .(bank_id, applied_qtr, loo_approval_rate)], by = "bank_id", all.x = TRUE)

# Build instrument that turns on after application quarter
bank[, z := ifelse(!is.na(applied_qtr) & quarter >= applied_qtr, loo_approval_rate, 0)]

# 2SLS: instrument treat with z
iv1 <- feols(risky_sec_share ~ 1 | bank_id + quarter | (treat ~ z) + ln_assets, 
             data = bank, cluster = ~ bank_id)
etable(iv1)

# 8) Robustness checks
# (a) Pre-trend test: leads in event study should be ~0
es_pretest <- es1 # already includes leads via sunab; plot
iplot(es1, ref.line = 0, main = "Event-study: risky securities share")

# (b) Applicant-only sample
bank_app <- bank[approval_status %in% c("approved","denied")]
es_app <- feols(risky_sec_share ~ sunab(g_index, q_index) + ln_assets | bank_id + quarter,
                data = bank_app, cluster = ~ bank_id)
etable(es_app)

# (c) Excluding markets with high treated penetration (HMDA)
hmda_mkt <- hmda[, .(treat_share = mean(treat, na.rm = TRUE)), by = .(county_fips, quarter)]
hmda2 <- merge(hmda, hmda_mkt, by = c("county_fips","quarter"))
hmda2_sub <- hmda2[treat_share < 0.3]
hmda_mod_rb <- feols(approve ~ treat*high_risk + high_risk + 
                       i(county_fips, quarter) + i(lender_id) + 
                       log(loan_amount) + log(pmax(applicant_income,1)) | 0,
                     data = hmda2_sub, cluster = ~ lender_id)
etable(hmda_mod_rb)


6. Expected Results

- Direction:
  - Risk-taking in flows: Positive. Treated banks will expand approval rates/loan sizes for riskier borrowers (HMDA) and originate a higher share of risky loan terms (DealScan). They will tilt investment portfolios toward higher-yield, higher-risk securities relative to controls.
  - Capital ratios: Increase mechanically after CPP.
  - Overall default risk: Ambiguous ex ante. Higher capital buffers reduce default risk; risk-shifting in assets increases it. My prior is that, on net over 4–8 quarters post-treatment, market-based distance-to-default (or z-score) improves modestly for average treated banks, but less so (or not at all) for banks that show the strongest risk substitution.
- Magnitudes (order of magnitude priors):
  - HMDA: Approval probability for high-risk segments rises by 2–5 percentage points relative to controls within county×quarter; loan amounts for risky borrowers increase 3–7%.
  - Securities risk: Risky securities share increases by 2–4 percentage points of total securities.
  - z-score: +0.1 to +0.3 SD for median treated bank; interaction shows smaller improvement (or none) for banks with the largest post-CPP increase in risky lending/investments.


7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment

For the primary DID/event-study design:
- C1: Parallel pre-trends supported by event-study leads and rich FE (bank and calendar-quarter; market×quarter at loan level) — 0.8
- C2: No meaningful anticipation (using funding date, excluding announcement window, checking leads) — 0.7
- C3: No time-varying confounders correlated with treatment after controls (other programs, regulator×time FE, county×time FE) — 0.7
- C4: Limited spillovers/SUTVA (tested via market-penetration robustness and excluding high-penetration markets) — 0.6
- C5: Stable measurement and composition (focus on flows, consistent lender-bank mapping, robust to trimming/extremes) — 0.9

For the secondary IV-DID:
- C1: Relevance (first-stage F-stat > 10 targeted) — 0.9
- C2: Exclusion (regulator propensity affects outcomes only through CPP) — 0.6
- C3: Monotonicity (no defiers) — 0.8
- C4: SUTVA (no interference via regulator shocks beyond CPP after FE) — 0.7
- C5: Correct functional form/instrument construction (cohort-month leave-one-out; regulator×quarter FE) — 0.8

Notes on implementation details and extensions
- Weighting: Re-estimate bank-level models weighting by lagged assets to reflect economic significance; show unweighted as baseline.
- Multiple-testing/false discovery: Pre-specify primary outcomes per domain (HMDA: approval probability for high-risk; DealScan: covenant-lite/unsecured; Investments: risky securities share; Default risk: z-score).
- Heterogeneity: By pre-CPP capital stringency (distance to “well-capitalized”), funding dose (CPP/Assets), and local house-price decline severity.
- Mediation: Decompose the total effect on default risk into contribution from capital ratio vs. asset risk using a mediation-style regression or Gelbach decomposition.
- Standard errors: Cluster at bank for bank-level; two-way cluster at lender and county (or borrower) for loan-level as robustness.

This plan provides a clear main identification design with internal tests of assumptions, plus an IV strategy to bolster causal claims against selection in approval and timing.
